document.title: uketsuke Initial Implementation Specification
document.purpose: Define the first dependable, FileTalk-based uketsuke implementation: receive jobs, dispatch them, report outcomes, and retire the work.
author: Lion Kimbro
Codex
depends-on: filetalk concept in Lion's Dictionary for LLMs

overview.summary: uketsuke is a small receptionist process for FileTalk jobs. It watches inbox/, accepts one job artifact at a time, dispatches the job to a registered handler, writes a response describing the result, and moves the completed job into retirement storage.
overview.name-meaning: uketsuke is treated as the receptionist at the front desk: it receives, routes, reports, and closes the record.
overview.initial-goal: Make one complete job lifecycle dependable and inspectable before adding richer routing, concurrency, or distributed coordination.
non-goals: A network service or socket-based broker.
A guarantee that arbitrary jobs are safe to execute.

design-principles: Filesystem is the transport boundary; no sockets or shared memory are required.
JSON is the initial message format and UTF-8 is the encoding.
A job file is an inspectable durable artifact, not merely an in-memory queue item.
External files are normalized and checked at the castle gate before dispatch.
The trusted interior operates on canonical job state.
Claiming a job is an atomic filesystem operation where the platform permits it.
Work is reported before it is retired.
Retirement preserves evidence; normal completion does not destroy the original job.
The first runtime is single-process and sequential unless a later specification changes this explicitly.

directories.inbox/: Unclaimed incoming job files. Producers write temporary files and atomically rename complete files into this directory.
directories.working/: Claimed job files currently being dispatched.
directories.outbox/: One response artifact for each accepted job, published by atomic rename after it is complete.
directories.retired/: Completed job records and lifecycle metadata, retained for inspection and replay analysis.
directories.dead-letter/: Jobs that cannot be normalized or whose lifecycle cannot be completed safely; never silently discarded.
directories.tmp/: Temporary files used while writing JSON or assembling an artifact; contents are not part of the public protocol.

file-naming.rule: Names must be deterministic from job-id and must not permit path traversal.

normal-flow: A producer writes a complete canonical job into inbox/ through a temporary file and atomic rename.
uketsuke discovers a JSON file in inbox/.
uketsuke validates the file and atomically moves it to working/; this is the claim.
uketsuke dispatches the claimed job to the handler selected by job-type.
uketsuke writes a response artifact to outbox/ through a temporary file and atomic rename.
uketsuke writes a retirement record and moves the claimed job from working/ into retired/.
The job is now retired and is not selected again during ordinary polling.
invalid-input-flow: If a discovered file is not readable JSON or cannot be normalized into a job, do not dispatch it.
Write an error response when a job-id can be identified.
Move the original artifact into dead-letter/ with a reason-bearing name.
If no safe job-id can be identified, preserve the artifact with a generated quarantine name and log the reason.
crash-recovery: A file in inbox/ is unclaimed and may be retried.
A file in working/ is claimed but not known to be complete; startup recovery must inspect it before retrying.
A response in outbox/ is considered published once its final filename exists.
A job in retired/ is not retried by default.
Recovery must never overwrite an existing response or retirement record without an explicit operator action.

dispatch.model: A local registry maps job-type strings to handlers.
dispatch.selection: The dispatcher selects exactly one handler from the canonical job's job-type.
dispatch.handler-contract: A handler receives the canonical current job as its one coherent record and returns a JSON-compatible result record, or raises an error that uketsuke converts into a failed outcome.
dispatch.initial-execution: Handlers run synchronously in the uketsuke process, one claimed job at a time.
dispatch.unknown-job-type: An unknown job-type is a failed job outcome, not an invalid transport message; it receives a response and is retired.
dispatch.handler-boundary: Handlers must not mutate inbox/, working/, outbox/, retired/, or dead-letter/ directly. The receptionist owns lifecycle movement and response publication.

operational-contract.polling: The process repeatedly scans inbox/ for completed JSON files. Poll interval and one-shot versus daemon mode are runtime configuration, not job semantics.
operational-contract.ordering: The initial implementation makes no global ordering promise. Within one scan, deterministic filename ordering is preferred.
operational-contract.idempotency: job-id is the identity key. Existing response or retirement artifacts are evidence that the lifecycle may already have completed and must be handled conservatively.
operational-contract.atomicity: All public JSON artifacts are written to tmp/ and atomically renamed into their final directory.
operational-contract.logging: Operational logs are append-only JSONL where implemented; the job response and retirement record remain the authoritative per-job outcome artifacts.
operational-contract.observability: At every lifecycle boundary, the filesystem should make it possible to determine whether a job is received, claimed, reported, retired, or quarantined.

response-semantics.success: The handler completed and returned a result accepted by uketsuke.
response-semantics.failure: The job was accepted and dispatched, but the handler or lifecycle operation failed.
response-semantics.rejected: The incoming artifact could not be normalized as a job and was quarantined without dispatch.
response-semantics.response-timing: The response is published before normal retirement is finalized.
response-semantics.result-preservation: The response may contain a concise result and diagnostics, but should not embed arbitrary non-JSON runtime objects or secrets.

recommended-modules: paths: configured directories and safe filename construction
files: UTF-8 JSON reads and atomic writes
dispatch: handler registration and current-job execution
receptionist: polling, claiming, reporting, and retirement machine
main: explicit startup and controlled process entrypoint
implementation-shape.machine-state: The receptionist module should expose a small g bundle for run state and a register for the current job. Internal lifecycle steps should be named zero-argument machine actions; arguments should represent caller-selected variation only.
implementation-shape.startup: No operational calls at import time. Registration, directory preparation, and polling begin from an explicit main() or init() path.
implementation-shape.classes: No classes are required for the initial implementation.

acceptance-criteria: A valid job placed into inbox/ is eventually claimed, dispatched, answered, and retired.
A handler result produces a valid response artifact with the same job-id.
A handler exception produces a failed response and does not crash the whole polling loop.
Malformed JSON is quarantined without dispatch and without silent deletion.
A partial public artifact is never treated as a complete incoming job.
A restart can distinguish inbox, working, outbox, retired, and dead-letter states.
Repeated polling does not ordinarily dispatch a retired job a second time.
Filesystem writes are UTF-8 and atomic at the public artifact boundary.
Tests cover successful dispatch, unknown job type, handler failure, malformed input, and recovery from interrupted lifecycle steps.
open-questions: What exact job types and built-in handlers should the first release provide?
Should handlers be Python callables only, subprocess commands, or both?
What is the authoritative timestamp format: ISO 8601 UTC, Unix seconds, or another convention?
Should response publication be sufficient for downstream consumers, or should an outbox delivery/acknowledgement lifecycle be added?
What operator action finalizes or replays a job stranded in working/?
Should the process expose one-shot and daemon modes in the first CLI?
What retention policy governs retired/ and dead-letter/?
Do job producers require a sender identity, correlation id, priority, or retry policy in v1?

job-id.description: Stable identity of one uketsuke job.
job-id.constraints: Non-empty safe identifier; must not contain path separators or traversal segments.

job-type.description: Registry key selecting the handler for a job.

timestamp.description: Creation or lifecycle time; exact representation remains an open question.

job.title: Uketsuke Job
job.description: The canonical JSON record accepted at the inbox boundary.

payload.type: object or other JSON-compatible value selected by job-type

response.title: Uketsuke Job Response
response.description: The durable outcome published for an accepted job.

vocabulary.rejected: Input could not be accepted as a job.

retirement-record.title: Uketsuke Retirement Record
retirement-record.description: Evidence that uketsuke finished the public lifecycle for a job.

notes: This is an initial implementation specification, not a complete FileTalk or workflow standard.
The inbox/ convention is specific to uketsuke and does not redefine FileTalk itself.
The specification intentionally leaves room for later job envelopes, subprocess handlers, retries, acknowledgements, and richer routing.
